title: Fractional model-version literals must be rejected before int() coercion
answers: version_number = 1.5 returns the wrong model version
fractional version number in model version search is silently truncated
why does searching model versions with a decimal version return version 1
model version filter accepts float literal
body:
Symptom: A model-version search with a fractional version_number (e.g. version_number = 1.5) returns a different version instead of an error.
Root cause: The filter parser returns a Python float for unquoted decimal literals, and int(1.5) silently yields 1. mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py:_get_search_model_versions_filter_clauses coerced the value with int() without checking the type first.
Fix pattern: Check isinstance(value, float) and raise INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE before the int(value) coercion. Quoted strings such as version_number='2' still go through int() and succeed.
Constraints: The guard is in the SQL store only. mlflow/utils/search_utils.py:SearchModelVersionUtils._does_model_version_match_clauses (FileStore path) still calls int() and can truncate, so backends may disagree. Reviewers flagged this as unresolved; do not assume parity across stores.
applies: Model-version search filter parsing in the SQLAlchemy model-registry store. Does not cover the run or MCP search paths.
says: Searching model versions with a decimal number returns the wrong model version.
Filtering model versions by a fractional number should display an invalid input error.
The model registry search box returns version one when searching for version one point five.
Decimal values entered in the model version filter are silently rounded down.
Reject fractional numbers entered into the model version search bar instead of returning results.
search: Model-version search filter parsing in the SQLAlchemy model-registry store must reject float literals before integer coercion. In mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py:_get_search_model_versions_filter_clauses, unquoted decimal floats must raise INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE via isinstance(value, float) before int(value) silently truncates them. Quoted integer strings like version_number='2' still pass through int() and succeed. This guard applies only to the SQLAlchemy store and excludes run or MCP search paths, while mlflow/utils/search_utils.py:SearchModelVersionUtils._does_model_version_match_clauses in FileStore still truncates.
